Built against [wamsoft/krkrz_dev](https://github.com/wamsoft/krkrz_dev) V2.6.5

A small release for 0.17.1:

- **A new opening for the sample**: the logo plays an opening movie of the sample's own, in its look: the K badge and the wordmark, the street with Ai coming in, three pictures from the demos and the evening title, over the start of "Daily Life", which it unlocks in the music room. It's an ordinary WebM without alpha, 14 s, with English and Japanese subtitles and a smaller version for phones; Replay's Movies tab shows a picture of it. `tools/assets/make_opening.py` draws it.
- **Movies fill the screen**: the smaller version of a movie that phones play (`<name>_sd`) showed at its own size in the middle of a black screen. `[movie]` now zooms a movie of another size to fill the screen, keeping its shape (`fit=false` keeps its own size), and `[image movie=... fit=true]` does the same on any layer. The smaller version also takes the full movie's subtitles.
- **A movie no longer hangs the game on a computer without a sound device**: there the engine can't start a movie's audio and holds a movie with sound at its first frame for ever, so the new opening, which has music, would have stopped the game at the logo. `[movie]` now ends a movie whose picture stops for 3 seconds.
- kagex-release 0.17.2 downloads the 0.17.2 engines

Known issue: the web build doesn't show movies yet. The browser's video player can't open a movie inside `data.xp3`, so on the web demo the opening ends after 3 s with nothing shown (as in 0.17.0 and 0.17.1).

Everything 0.17.0 added (settings laid out from one table, reading settings, the hero's name, the name box, on-screen indicators, movies with subtitles, the credits roll, writers' shorthands and `[vo]`, the Extras touches, Android manifest additions in kagex-release) is in [0.17.0's notes](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/releases/tag/0.17.0), and 0.17.1's fixes in [its notes](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/releases/tag/0.17.1).

The sample game with Live2D (`kagex_sample_live2d_<platform>`, added to this release once it's out) holds Live2D's Cubism Core: by installing or playing it you agree not to copy the Cubism Core out of it, distribute it apart from the game, modify it, or reverse engineer, decompile or disassemble it. It uses sample data owned and copyrighted by Live2D Inc.

Everything in this release is listed in [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/krkren/kagex/blob/0.17.2/CHANGELOG.md).

On Windows the engine needs OpenGL ES: a graphics driver that supports it, or ANGLE's `libEGL.dll` and `libGLESv2.dll` next to `krkrz.exe`.

The macOS app and tools aren't signed with an Apple Developer ID, so macOS blocks them the first time: open the app from the context menu (Open), or allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security; for the tools, `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine kagex-release kagex-lipsync`. The Android APK is signed with a debug key: allow installs from unknown sources, or use `adb install`. The sample's iOS build is for the Simulator; kagex-release signs a game for iPhones and iPads with your own Apple Developer certificate.
